items.title: Commissioners’ Notice of Public Hearing – Vacate Drainage and Utility Easement on October 12, 2026
items.text: NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING REGARDING THE VACATION OF DRAINAGE AND UTILITY EASEMENT On October 12, 2026, at 10:00 A.M., the Johnson County Board of Commissioners will hold a public hearing regarding Ordinance 2026-O-10: An Ordinance Vacating a Drainage and Utility Easement. The Commissioners will consider the vacation of a drainage and utility easement contained within Lots 36 and 37 in the Final Plat of Water’s Edge, Section Three, an addition in Johnson County, as per the plat thereof recorded in Instrument 2025-010117, in the of ice of the Recorder of Johnson County, Indiana. This addition is north of the intersection of Lakeview Dr and Waters Edge Way. The hearing will be held at the West Annex Auditorium, 86 West Court Street, Franklin, IN 46131. Dated this 29th day of September, 2026 Board of Commissioners Johnson County, Indiana

Board & Commission Openings
The Town of Edinburgh has several openings on various 2027 boards and commissions starting October 5, 2026.
· Planning Commission- one board member for a 4-year term. Qualified applicants must live within Town limits and be an elected official or an employee of the Town of Edinburgh.
· Board of Metropolitan Police Commissioners- one board member for a 3-year term. Qualified applicants live within Town limits.
· Joint Planning Commission- 2 board members for a 3-year term. Qualified applicants must live within Town limits.
· Edinburgh Redevelopment Commission- 6 board members for a 1-year term. Qualified applicants must live within Town limits.
· Economic Development Board- 2 board members; 1 board member for a 1-year term and 1 board member for a 2-year term. Qualified applicants must live within Town limits.

items.title: Town of Whiteland: Board of Zoning Appeals
items.text:
The Whiteland Advisory Board of Zoning Appeals (“BZA”) works to ensure that zoning regulations are fairly applied across varying properties in town. Essentially, the BZA serves as a board to hear appeals that specific zoning regulations should be applied differently to a particular property due to certain conditions of the site or the proposed use. The administrative appeal is an appeal of a decision made by town staff regarding the zoning code. The BZA does not enforce the zoning code, but they can adjust the regulations for a property to suit its specific site conditions that would otherwise be in violation of the zoning code. The responsibilities of the BZA is as follows:
Indiana Code provides that the BZA has the following specific authorities:
Granting of variances Developmental standards variances Variances of use
Developmental standards variances
Variances of use
Granting of special exceptions (also known as conditional uses)
Appeals from administrative decisions
Members
Two members of the BZA are selected from the Plan Commission, two are appointed by the Town Council President, and one is appointed by the Town Council. By state code, members cannot hold any other elected or appointed position (except the two Plan Commission members).

items.text: Page 1 of 12 GREENWOOD COMMON COUNCIL ORDINANCE NO. 26-34 AN ORDINANCE FIXING SALARIES OF APPOINTED OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES OF THE CITY OF GREENWOOD, INDIANA AND CITY UTILITIES FOR THE YEAR 2027 WHEREAS, pursuant to Ind. Code § 36 -4-7-3, the Mayor shall fix the compensation of each appointive officer, deputy, and other employee of the city in departments other than the police and fire department, subject to approval by the legislative body; WHEREAS, pursuant to Ind. Code § 36 -4-7-3(d), the Clerk may fix the salaries of the deputies and employees of her department, subject to approval by the legislative body; WHEREAS, as head of the City’s judicial branch, the City Court Judge may fix the salaries of the Court, subject to approval by the legislative body; WHEREAS, pursuant to Ind. Code § 36 -4-7-4, the administrative agencies operating the City’s utilities shall fix the amount of compensation for utility employees, subject to the approval of the Mayor and legislative body; WHEREAS, pursuant to Ind. Code § 36 -4-7-5, salaries of city officers and employees shall be scheduled as provided in the budget classification prescribed by the State Board of Accounts; WHEREAS, pursuant to Ind. Code § 36-8-3-3(d), the annual compensation of all members of the police and fire departments and other appointees shall be fixed by ordinance of the legislative body; WHEREAS, pursuant to Ind. Code § 36-10-3-10(b), the Park and Recreation Board shall fix the salaries of the employees of the Park and Recreation Department subject to the provisions of Ind. Code §§ 36-4-7-5 and 6; WHEREAS, pursuant to Ind. Code § 8-22-2-5(b)(2), the Board of Aviation Commissioners shall fix the compensation of Airport employees subject to appropriations made by the fiscal body of the entity; WHEREAS, the Mayor, the Clerk, the Judge, the Board of Public Works and Safety, the Park and Recreation Board, Board of Directors of the Department of Stormwater Management, and the Board of Aviation Commissioners have exercised their statutory duties and have fixed the below maximum salaries for each position outlined, including a one year premium pay; and WHEREAS, the Common Council has reviewed the proposed fixed salaries and found them to be in the best interest of the City; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE COMMON COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF GREENWOOD, INDIANA, AS FOLLOWS: Section 1. The City fund(s) from which compensation is to be paid is indicated following each salary or wage rate. The funds are abbreviated as follows: General Fund (“GF”), Sewage Works Operating (“SWO”), Storm Water Utility (“SW”), Motor Vehicle Highway (“MVH”), Waste Management (“WM”), Park (“P”), Fire (“F”), Clerk’s Records Perpetuation Fund (“CR”), Special Non-Reverting (“SNR”), and Aviation Operation (“A”). Bi-weekly salaries are listed for full time employees. Hourly wage rates are listed for part-time and seasonal employees. Section 2. The following amounts representing a maximum salary to be paid as compensation for full time appointed officers and employees for the City of Greenwood, Indiana and its utilities are hereby established as set forth below. The actual pay for each position is to be determined by the administration in collaboration with human resources and each department head. Said salaries shall be paid on a bi-weekly basis. No increase in compensation shall be effective until the City budget, tax rate, and tax levy for the 2027 budget year has been fixed in compliance with Ind. Code § 6-1.1-17-5 and Ind. Code § 36-4-7-11. In accordance with the federal Fair Labor Standards Act (“FLSA”), each position is classified as exempt (“E”) or non -exempt (“NE”). Non -exempt employees shall be entitled to receive overtime compensation in accordance with the FLSA and Greenwood Municipal Code § 2-78(b). Exempt employees shall be entitled to receive compensatory time in accordance with Greenwood Municipal Code § 2-78(a). All full-time employees shall be entitled to receive City benefits in accordance with Chapter 2, Article 8 of the Greenwood Municipal Code. The following maximum amounts to be paid as compensation for appointed board and commission members for the City of Greenwood, Indiana and its utilities are hereby established as set forth below. VARIOUS BOARDS AND COMMISSIONS Board/Commission # of Members Fund Fund Compensation per meeting ATTENDED Board of Aviation Commissioners 4 A $35.00 Board of Public Works & Safety (50/50) 3 GF SS $501.56 bi-weekly Planning Commission 8 GF $125.00 Board of Zoning Appeals 4 GF $125.00 Economic Development Commission 5 GF $75.00 Board of Parks and Recreation 4 P $125.00 Police Merit Commission 5 GF $75.00 Redevelopment Commission+ 5 GF $150.00 Board of Directors of Department of Storm Water Management 3 SW $150.00 Fire Department Merit Commissioners 5 F $75.00 + A Redevelopment Commission Member who holds a lucrative office for the purpose of Article 2, Section 9 of the Indiana Constitution is not entitled to, and shall not receive, compensation or per diem for serving on the Redevelopment Commission Section 5. Prior to February 15, 20 27, employees, with the exception of merit members of the Greenwood Police Department and Greenwood Fire Department, hired on or before December 31, 2013, shall be paid longevity pay of $75.00 per year of service in accordance with Greenwood Municipal Code § 2-67. Section 6. The following schedule of Technical Specialty Compensation shall be available to members of the Greenwood Fire Department as determined by the Fire Chief: (a) Any member of the Fire Department that meets the requirements of Fire/Arson Investigation team of the Greenwood Fire Department may be compensated up to $200.00 in 2027 - as determined by the Fire Chief. (b) Any member of the Fire Department that meets the requirements of the Greenwood Fire Department Honor Guard may be compensated up to $600.00 in 2027 - as determined by the Fire Chief. (c) Any member of the Fire Department that holds a State of Indiana Paramedic license may be compensated up to $3,250 as determined by the Fire Chief. (d) Any member of the Fire Department that serves as PPE Gear Master may be compensated up to $925.00 in 2027 - as determined by the Fire Chief. (e) Any administrative assistant who serves as the recording secretary for the Merit Commission, Local Pension Board, or other assigned Boards may be compensated up to $350 .00 per board, as determined by the Fire Chief. (f) Any member of the Fire Department that meets the requirements of SWAT Team Medic may be compensated up to $1,000.00 in 2027 – as determined by the Chief. Section 7. Annual and bi-weekly salaries for Fire Marshal, Deputy Fire Marshal, Support Services Coordinator, and Administrative Assistant in the Fire Department are for 40 hours worked per week and shall be compensated at the employee's regular hourly rate as defined in the FLSA; hours worked in excess of 40 hours per week shall be compensated at 1.5 times the employee's regular hourly rate as defined in the FLSA. Section 8. Annual and bi -weekly salaries for Probationary Firefighters/EMT, First Class Firefighters/EMT, Engineer, Shift Lieutenants, Captains, and Battalion Chiefs are for all hours up to 212 hours worked per 28 day work period. Hours worked in excess of 212 hours per 28 day work period shall be compensated at 1.5 times the employee’s regular hourly rate as defined in the FLSA. Ord. 26-34 Page 10 of 12 Section 9. Firefighter/EMT Probationary firefighters will be eligible to receive a one-time payment of $5,000.00 upon achieving certification and completing no less than 6 months of employment in the case of non-certified probationers, or upon completing no less than 6 months of employment for certified probationers, as approved by the Fire Chief. Additionally, there will be no salary increases permitted during the probationary period. Section 10. Annual and bi-weekly salaries for law enforcement personnel in the Police Department are for up to 168 hours worked per 28 day work period. Hours worked in excess of 160 hours, up to 171 hours, per 28 day work period shall be compensated with one hour of other compensatory time (as defined by the FLSA) per hour worked or paid at the employee’s regular hourly rate as determined by the Police Chief and internal policies and procedures of the Police Department. Hours worked in excess of 171 hours per 28 day work period shall be compensated at 1.5 times the employee’s regular hourly rate as defined in the FLSA. Section 11. The following schedule of Technical Specialty Compensation shall be available to members of the Greenwood Police Department as determined by the Police Chief: (a) First class officers who serve as field training officers may be eligible for additional compensation in the amount of $2,0 00.00 per year as determined by the Police Chief. The Field Training Coordinator may also be eligible for this compensation as determined by the Police Chief. (b) Honor Guard members, K -9 Officers, Motorcycle Officers, SWAT members, Drone pilots and Hostage Negotiators may be eligible for additional compensation in the amount of $1,000.00 per year as determined by the Police Chief. (c) SWAT commander may be eligible for additional compensation in the amount of $ 2,000.00 per year as determined by the Police Chief. Section 12. Members of the Greenwood Police Department that are required to be “on call” during their regularly scheduled time off, may be eligible for compensation of $35 per day as determined by the Police Chief. Section 13. The annual and bi-weekly salaries for all other non-exempt positions listed herein are for up to a 40 hour work week. Hours worked in excess of 40 hours worked per week shall be compensated at 1.5 times the employee’s regular hourly rate as defined in the FLSA. Section 14. The Aquatics Manager position may be eligible for a pay out of compensatory time earned rather than utilizing it as paid time off in the discretion of the Director of Parks and Recreation and Deputy Mayor depending upon budget and scheduling needs. No other position in the City shall be so eligible Section 15. Any full -time grounds maintenance supervisor/worker who holds a valid C ertified Playground Safety Inspector (CPSI) certificate on January 1 of the current fiscal year shall be paid a once per year bonus payment of $500 .00. Timing of payment shall be in accordance with timing of city longevity bonuses, and employee will only be eligible if still employed by the Parks Department on the prescribed payment date. Section 16. Any full-time Building Commissioner, Field Inspector, and Building Inspector in the Department of Community Development Services is eligible to receive $500.00 in certification pay for additional certifications earned during the year, up to a maximum of two certifications per year. This payment will be made upon submission of certification by the department head to the Finance Department Office Manager and Payroll Administrator. Section 17. All requests to increase pay above the budgeted amount for a position will require review and approval by the City Controller and the Mayor’s Office. Failure to have both of these approvals will result in denial of the increase request. Section 18. The sections, paragraphs, sentences, clauses, phrases and words of this Ordinance are separable, and if any word, phrase, clause, sentence, paragraph or section of this Ordinance shall be declared unconstitutional, invalid or unenforceable by the valid judgment or decree of a Court of competent jurisdiction, such unconstitutionality, invalidity or unenforceability shall not affect any of the remaining words, phrases, clauses, sentences, paragraphs and sections of this Ordinance. Section 19. This ordinance shall be in full force and effect after its passage, approval and publication according to law. Code § 36 -4-7-2 the Common Council shall, by ordinance, fix the annual compensation of all elected city officers; NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE COMMON COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF GREENWOOD, INDIANA: Section 1. The City fund(s) from which compensation is to be paid is the General Fund. Section 2. That from and after the first day of January 20 27, the salary and pay schedule for the City Judge of the City of Greenwood, Indiana, continuing until duly changed, shall be fixed as follows: Position # of Positions Bi-Weekly Salary Fund GF City Court Judge 1 $4,798.53 100% Section 3. That from and after the first day of January 20 27, the City Judge may receive, in addition to the above salary, the following additional compensation. a) The City Judge may receive reimbursement for actual direct expenses, including reimbursement for miles traveled on City business in a personal vehicle at the rate established pursuant to written Board of Public Works and Safety Resolutions and meals and lodging incurred while attending seminars, conferences, workshops pursuant to written Board of Public Works and Safety Resolutions, and other business which promotes the betterment of the City and furthers the education and training of City officials in accordance with Greenwood Municipal Code Sec. 2-96 and which are consistent with audit positions of the State Board of Accounts. b) The City Judge is generally eligible to receive other benefits that are available to City employees. Section 4. That this Ordinance shall be in full force and effect after its passage and approval according to law. Stones Crossing Road, generally located along the west side of N. County Road 125 West south of Pleasant Crossing Elementary School, within the corporate boundaries of the City of Greenwood, from the current zoning of AG – Agricultural District to RM – Residential - Medium Lot Zone, to allow for the development of a single-family residential subdivision; WHEREAS, the Commission requested, and the Owner agreed to, the following commitments regarding the use and development of said real estate: 1. Trails shall be designed and constructed in accordance with the Greenwood Future Trail Network Map and applicable trail standards in the Comprehensive Plan and UDO. 3. The internal trail network shall be a robust trail system to form a loop or consistent path, and implemented in agreement with and subject to approval from City Planning Staff. 4. Internal trails shall connect to the Lawrence Drive trail at a location along the eastern frontage in addition to the northern connection. 5. The applicant shall dedicate one additional right-of-way for street stubs connecting the proposed subdivision street network to adjoining west AND at least one to the south vacant or underdeveloped land. items.text: Meeting of the Greenwood Common Council MINUTES Date: September 21, 2026 Time: 7:00 pm Place: Council Chamber 300 S Madison Ave Greenwood, Indiana I. Call Meeting to Order A. Pledge of Allegiance B. Prayer: David Denny - lay leader at Victory Baptist Church C. Roll Call: Council Members Present: Mike Campbell ("Mr. Campbell"), Linda Gibson ("Ms. Gibson"), Ezra Hill ("Mr. Hill"), David Hopper ("Mr. Hopper"), Erin Kasch ("Ms. Kasch"), David Lekse, ("Mr. Lekse"), Teri Manship, ("Ms. Manship"), Steve Moan ("Mr. Moan") Darin Hoggatt ("Mr. Hoggatt") City Officials: Mark Myers (“Mayor Myers”) Jeannine Myers ("Ms. Myers") Clerk, Greg Wright ("Mr. Wright") Controller, Sam Hodson (“Mr. Hodson”) Corporation Council, James Ison ("Chief Ison") Police Chief, Jayme Washel (“Chief Washel”) Fire Chief, Drew Foster (“Judge Foster”) City Judge, and Department Heads. Council President Campbell reminded attendees that respectful participation is expected and that disruptions are not permitted. This will be read before each meeting: Before we begin, I want to remind everyone that respectful participation is expected. We welcome public input at the appropriate times, but there will be no yelling or interruptions that prevent the meeting from moving forward. Anyone who disrupts the meeting will be asked to leave and may be escorted out. II. Approval of Minutes A. Minutes from the regular meeting September 9 ,2026 Motion to approve regular meeting minutes from September 9, 2026 by Kasch, seconded by Hill Votes: Ayes – Campbell, Gibson, Hill, Hopper Kasch Abstain: Lekse, Manship, Moan, Hoggatt Motion Passes: 5-0 with 4 abstentions III. Reports A. Corporation Counsel B. Controller C. Committee & Board Report IV. Public Comments This timeslot is for residents who would like to address the Council about matters on the agenda. All materials presented at a public meeting are considered part of the official record; please provide a copy to the Clerk. Individuals- 5-minute time limit; Groups- 20-minute time limit Deann Lautenbach, 2255 S. Franklin Rd, Greenwood, IN 46143 I live at the corner of Franklin and Clark Road in Greenwood. I'm an aggravated and affected neighbor due to living in the middle of the unfinished corridor between 65 and 74, which will be feeding an enormous amount of traffic to the destination travel center, being one of the largest gas stations in the entire state of Indiana. I am here tonight to establish a formal legally binding administrative record against docket PC 2026-035. To fully preserve my right to file a judicial review in the Johnson County courts. I request that this Council table this back to the Planning Commission or deny this petition because it creates a severe procedural violation, breaks local ordinances, and creates a textbook, arbitrary, capricious action. Indiana open door law. Under Indiana Code Section 5.14 1.55, public agencies are required to give public notice of their meetings, including posting an agenda if one is utilized at least 48 hours in advance, excluding weekends and legal holidays, dropping a major, unvetted, supplemental traffic study on a Friday afternoon for a Monday vote, actively circumvents the transparency mandated by the state sunshine law. Greenwood Planning Division staff report ruled: after an examination of information in the public record and findings from additional research, staff shall publish a technical review committee report that provides an analysis of the petition request. Such reports shall be published along with an agenda approximately five days prior to the meeting. By failing to give a five-day buffer, the city directly broke its own local guidelines. Indiana Code Section 3674607. This statute dictates that any zoning ordinance or planned unit development text amendment must follow a strict process between the Planning Commission and the Legislative Council. Under Indiana Land Use law, if a developer introduces significant technical updates or modifications after the Planning Commission has already voted, the Common Council is legally required to remand the proposal back to the Planning Commission. This ensures that the public hearing body can officially investigate, review, and certify the new data before a final vote takes place. Indiana Code Section 3674604. This statute mandates that a major zoning ordinance or text amendment cannot be legally enacted without a formal, legally advertised public hearing because the brand-new September 15th traffic memo reveals a severe level of service F gridlock. Failures right at our local school entrances, avenues, and because this data was hidden from the public portal until Friday afternoon, the community has never been granted a valid public hearing on the actual material facts of this case. I gave you guys all exhibits. Exhibit A: The build, this is from the traffic study, build 2037 capacity reports from Section F, all the traffic study. This document proves that the intersection of Emerson Avenue and Worthsville Road will suffer complete gridlock during peak morning school hours. The northbound approach drops to a level of service grade F, forcing parents, teachers, and school buses to face a catastrophic average delay of 275.26 seconds, which is over four and a half minutes. Of forced idling per vehicle. This extensive line of cars will stack directly backward during the morning peak hour, clogging the entrance avenues of Clark Pleasant Middle School and creating a dangerous hazard gridlock where student commuters are trapped in stationary traffic. Exhibit B: The existing 2026 plus site capacity reports from Section D of the study. This proves that the infrastructure will fail on day one. The very moment this site opens, page two reveals that the southbound approach directly exiting the Grassy Creek Elementary School access road completely breaks down into an immediate level of service F, forcing parents and school buses to idle for 74.9 seconds, over a minute each just to exit the school gates. Furthermore, page four exposed a catastrophic four-way systematic breakdown at county roads. 200 East and Worthsville Road, where the northbound and southbound approaches simultaneously fail at level service F, blocking up primary school access road with immediate delays up to three and a half minutes. Exhibit C, and I have more, but I can't. proving the developers actively breaking our local laws to circumvent safety protections, unifying development ordinances section 100107 with the illegal spot zoning. That's going on. I need to put that in the record so I can file a judicial review. Furthermore, your master plan used on table 17 completely bans travel plazas. That is illegal spot zoning. The developer is also proposing to remove an active timed travel traffic signal along the corridor and replace it with a roundabout element, eliminating the only mechanical guarantee that stops commercial traffic to let parents in school buses. Thank you. Kim Crawford, 166 Caplinger Place, Greenwood, In 46143 I am also the school board president for the Clark Pleasant Community School Corporation. Council President, Council Members, and City staff, thank you for the opportunity to speak this evening. I am here on behalf of the Clark Pleasant Community School Corporations and the families we serve. We appreciate the city and Buc-ee’s for conducting an initial traffic study and for sharing the updated remote this last week. We're not opposed to the development. However, we do have significant concerns about what the updated study demonstrates and the limited scope of the proposed mitigations. Our responsibility is to ensure that any changes along Worthsville Road support safe, reliable operations for our students, families, and our bus drivers. The updated Buc-ee’s traffic study provides new data on projected traffic volumes and interception performance during school drop-off and pickup windows. Although the city concludes that the site “does not result in significant additional traffic impacts during school- related peak periods,” several findings, including our own observations, indicate meaningful concerns for school operations and student safety. First, school peak traffic is already operating at a near rush-hour intensity. PM drop-off volumes are only about 50 vehicles lower than evening rush-hour peak. Because these peaks do not overlap, Buc-ee’s traffic represents additional load, not shared load. Second, the multiple intersections show significant delay growth between current conditions and 2037 projections. Worthsville and Emerson (northbound) shows substantial increases in delay in the report. Worthsville and Southlake (southbound) already experiences significant drop-off delays and it's projected to nearly double. Worthsville Road and County Road 200 shows delays exceeding 120 seconds or two minutes today- both AM southbound and PM northbound with worsening delays projected. These are the same intersections that our buses and our student drivers and our families use in order to get to the middle school and the two elementary schools there. Third Buc-ee’s is projected to add 1,045 trips during the morning drop-off and 1,380 trips during afternoon pickup. The study attempts to differentiate where these trips go afterwards, but the impact occurs the moment we enter the roadway, Worthsville Road. During compressed school windows, any added volume destabilizes flow. Fourth, only one mitigation has been proposed, re-striving at the southbound approach at Worthsville Road and Ray Crowe Way. And this is the entrance to the middle school. No other improvements have been recommended for intersections already showing severe delays. If striking Ray Crowe Way was the solution, we would have thought about it and would have done it before now. Finally, despite these findings, the study concludes that Buc-ee's does not result in significant additional traffic impacts during school-related periods. This conclusion does not align with the data that was presented or with school-specific traffic behavior. Because of these concerns, the district respectfully requests a formal commitment from the city and Buc-ee’s. If Buc-ee's operations create significant negative impact on our instructional day, bus routing our on-time performance, or parent pickup and drop-off operations, we just asking that the city and Buc-ee’s re-engage with us collaboratively to identify and implement mitigation strategies, including additional studies or infrastructure improvements. There's very little we can do on our own without more help. Our focus is simple: to ensure that the daily experience of our students, families, and staff remains safe and predictable as this progress progresses. We value our partnership with the city and Buc- ee’s and we want to continue to work together constructively. Thank you for your time and attention. I appreciate Scott Ratcliffe, who is one of the senior engineers for Buc-ee’s, for producing the revised traffic study. To me and to us as a school corporation last week. I appreciate them willing to redo the traffic study that last week of August. President Crawford just said a lot of similar points. I'll reiterate a few of them, but not to be repetitive and for the sake of brevity. I do want to emphasize some of those key areas that are of concern to us with the traffic flow That would be Worthsville & Emerson, Worthsville & South Lake Avenue, and Worthsville & County Rd 200 The one suggestion to obviously reach strike the left and turn lanes that's on our property right by middle school entrance. Appreciate that. We could do that. Signage, we could do that. My final request would be: as Buc-ee’s is built, I would love to see improved and stronger communication from all entities because, as it's built and even as it opens up, whatever that timeframe is, and the impact that it will have on our school day is so significant. I would love to work together with, again, all entities because it's important that obviously we conduct school. I've made our Department of Education aware of this. And so, the goal is for us, to work with you, not to be against you, but to make sure that we have school every single day within the required hours that were allotted. Thank you for your time. Updating the comprehensive plan involves not only community input, hiring the third-party companies of HWC Engineering and Stantec. The project siphoned $200,000 from the city budget. The plan says it is critical that this area holds a strong set of development criteria to ensure new development allows the city to grow its tax base, of course, but also to protect adjacent rural lifestyles. The new plan acknowledges Greenwood residents expressed their concern throughout the process about industrial development continuing south past Worthsville Road. Additionally, the HWC Steering Committee held a meeting specifically addressing the future land use of this area. The very first bullet point meeting states: “Areas surrounding the I-65 and Worthsville Road interchange should remain largely residential with limited commercial uses that serve the surrounding neighborhoods and not those traveling along the highway.” There are two major issues regarding this land and its proposed use. First, the community repeatedly expressed its concern about industrial and warehouse development in the area. Similar projects in the area have not come to fruition because the city listened to the residents and honored their promise to prevent industrial developments. But it's important to note that the problem with proposed industrial developments in the past was not with the business of logistics itself. Rather, it is what those businesses bring to the land: massive structures, invasive lighting, and daunting amounts of traffic. Though not in the business of logistics, a Buc-ee’s brings all of those things front and center, industrial or not. Even though they themselves clearly thought that their operations warranted industrial classifications when they originally brought this before the APC. The spirit of no warehouses and no industrial was to guard against these types of developments. Secondly, allowing this development or any like it will destroy the vision for Greenwood Crossing. The plan calls for a development that is harmonious with residential development on adjacent properties. However, a 120-pump gas station is a poisoned pill. It spoils the land around it. What it shows here is there's a radius of 2,500 feet from the proposed site. The distance that in our plan is supposed to be residential. And when you look at that, you will see that there is no new housing development in any of those 37. Maybe some was existing, but nothing new. All that comes afterwards is warehouses and other large-scale development buildings. Every Buc-ee’s dead zone is a far cry from what Greenwood Crossing is supposed to be, from what we spent $200,000 to plan, and from what this Council promised was in our future.
